evidence: 'The Bridge' (1986) was produced by Marley Marl for MC Shan, released on Cold Chillin', and entered the Billboard Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart, as recorded in standard hip-hop histories and the two men's own accounts.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: 'The Bridge' is a proud, unhurried borough anthem, MC Shan naming names and places over Marl's beat. 'The Bridge Is Over', KRS-One's answer a year later, borrows the same title and subject and turns it into an attack, faster and meaner, ending with a mocking sung outro aimed straight at Shan and Marl. Same beat-and-borough format, opposite intent.

explanation.age7: Marley Marl made the music for MC Shan's song about his neighbourhood, Queensbridge. Another rapper thought it was bragging too much and wrote an angry song back.
explanation.age13: Marley Marl produced MC Shan's 'The Bridge' (1986), telling the story of their Queensbridge crew. Many listeners heard it as claiming Queensbridge invented hip-hop, and the Bronx's KRS-One answered with 'South Bronx' and then 'The Bridge Is Over', starting the Bridge Wars.
explanation.adult: A straightforward production credit whose consequence, not its content, is the interesting part: this record's reception, not its actual lyrics, is what launched hip-hop's first well-documented borough rivalry.
